summary.text: Lynn Hammel is the Republican candidate for the Iowa House of Representatives, District 33, in the November 3, 2026 general election, in a race with no incumbent against Democrat Ivette Muhammad.
A network engineer who lives on Des Moines's East Side, he says he is running on property tax relief, public safety and support for working families.

paragraphs.text: Lynn Hammel's listed profession is information technology.
In a Ballotpedia survey, Hammel said he grew up on a small dairy farm in Northeast Iowa, worked on the farm, delivered newspapers and worked as a farmhand, and paid his way through college.

He said he moved to Des Moines in 1995, is a longtime member of Northridge Baptist Church where he has served as a deacon and treasurer, has served as treasurer of the Fairmont Park Neighborhood Association, and founded BarrelsIowa.com to encourage water conservation.
Hammel advanced from the Republican primary on June 2, 2026.

In the survey, he described himself as a husband and father of five and not a career politician, and he named property tax relief, protecting victims and strengthening public safety, and standing up for workers and working families as his three key messages.
